reasons: Classification is correct: p0149 imposes a blanket consent requirement on Licensee with no affiliate/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard while leaving Licensor unrestricted (fails the mutual-notice fallback), and p0134 gives Licensor an automatic termination right on Licensee's Change of Control — expressly walk-away territory under the rule.

Redline reaches the preferred position with targeted edits: affiliate/successor carve-out plus 'not unreasonably withheld' standard for Licensee, mirrored consent limit and no-competitor bar on Licensor, and deletion of the change-of-control termination trigger replaced by post-closing notice.

Internal coherence preserved: p0149's cross-reference to the Change of Control section still resolves to the rewritten p0134, which now states a Change of Control is not an assignment and requires no consent, and the trailing 'CHANGE OF CONTROL means:' lead-in is retained so the downstream definition is not orphaned.

Advisory minimal-edit failures (0.74 / 0.83 changed-character ratios) are justified here — deleting an automatic termination trigger and adding both a carve-out and a mutual consent standard necessarily rewrites most of each sentence; no gratuitous drafting was introduced beyond extending the reasonableness qualifier to the existing assign/sublicense/transfer sentence.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position, and correctly explains both the carve-out and the removal of the vendor exit right.
